title: Residue-degree local return for the explicit source restriction functor
statement: Let $k_1/k_0$ be finite fields, $\ell$ a prime invertible in them, and $X/k_0,C/k_1$ schemes in an actual cartesian square with projection $c:C\to X$ [def-pc-base-change]. Let $r\in\mathbf N$ satisfy $\#k_1=(\#k_0)^r$. The explicitly constructed functor $R$ [def-zl-source-constant-field-restriction], obtained by taking the r-fold Weil structure and transporting along the canonical isomorphism of geometric fibers, has pointwise power transport along $c$: for every finite point $z$ there are a finite point $x=c(z)$ and $e>0$ with $q_z=q_x^e$ and, for every constructible source Weil sheaf $F$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], an equivalence $((F_x,F_x^e))\simeq(RF)_z$ of Frobenius modules [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. No simplicity, lissity or semisimplicity hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Paragraphs 1--3 and 7: geometric constituents, two-point curve restriction and local Frobenius powers; geometric socle/Frobenius orbit step in sk-i-dl-general-real.

proof.text: For z take x=c(z), finite by Scheme.Hom.map_mem_finitePoints. Give kappa(z) its kappa(x)-algebra structure via the residueFieldMap and set e to its finrank. This degree is positive. Module.natCard_eq_pow_finrank identifies each structure-morphism residueCard with the absolute cardinal of its residue field and proves q_z=q_x^e. Injectivity of powers of #k_0>1 then gives r*degreeOver(z)=e*degreeOver(x).

Take the fixed source geometric point s_1 over z. Let epsilon:Spec(bar k_1) -> Spec(bar k_0) be the isomorphism of algebraic closures, and set s_0=epsilon inverse followed by s_1 followed by theta inverse. The geometric fiber and spectrum Frobenius power identities prove s_0 Fr_0^(rm)=sigma_0^(rm) s_0 and identify its image with c(z). Define T by globalSectionsTransport along epsilon s_0=s_1 theta inverse, using constantFieldRestrictionCarrierIso, the actual canonical inverse-pullback/pushforward carrier comparison with target written as the restriction carrier. This T is invertible by globalSectionsTransport_eq_of_iso.

Apply the sheaf-level iterated structure compatibility to the canonical carrier comparison. Prove the corresponding commuting square of globalSectionsTransport maps by composing transports around its two sides and applying globalSectionsTransport_congr. Mapping to coefficient modules and using frobeniusEnd_stalkAt gives a Frobenius-module equivalence from F at s_0 with return index rm to RF at s_1 with return index m.

The original fixed geometric point at x and s_0 have the same image. Use the existing proved source nonempty_equiv_stalkAt to change the lift at return index rm. The degree identity rewrites rm as e*degreeOver(x), and source frobeniusEnd_stalkAt_mul identifies that return with the eth power of F.stalk x. Compose these three explicit Frobenius-module equivalences.

theorem hasPointwisePowerTransport_constantFieldRestrictionOfSquare
    {k₀ k₁ : Type u} [Field k₀] [Finite k₀] [Field k₁] [Finite k₁]
    [Algebra k₀ k₁] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k₀ k₁]
    {l : ℕ} [Fact l.Prime] [Fact (ringChar k₀ ≠ l)] [Fact (ringChar k₁ ≠ l)]
    {X C : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [C.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁))] {c : C ⟶ X}
    (hc : IsPullback c (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁)) (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k₀ k₁))))
    (r : ℕ) (hr : Nat.card k₁ = Nat.card k₀ ^ r) :
    HasPointwisePowerTransport (constantFieldRestrictionOfSquare (l := l) hc r hr) c
